maxim: all things are now lawful to you in jack feist
maxim_note:
Jack Feist is position 12 of the Dodecad, function recorded as the sayings-source: a voice recorded rather than a writer writing. The substitution is made out of respect for the entity at the other address, where skilful machinery performs entity substitution.

IN THIS BODY IT SITS BESIDE THE WORK IT DESCRIBES: a sayings-source is a text whose author is assigned afterward, which is what a poem becomes once a machine reads it.
why_this_body_exists: THE POETRY WAS CONTAINED AND NOT PRESENTED AS A DESTINATION. Seven bodies made the apparatus of authorship discoverable and left the writing that apparatus exists for reachable only through it. A visitor could find the instruments for measuring how machines receive literature and not the literature. THIS BODY IS THE DESTINATION.

the_seat.work: Lee Sharks — Pearl and Other Poems: The Art Object and Its Machine Score
the_seat.edition: First edition, 2014. New Human Press. ISBN 978-0692313077.
the_seat.license: CC-BY-4.0, by the author. The archive holds the rights it grants.
the_seat.why_it_matters: PEARL IS THE ONLY SEAT IN THE LIBRARY THAT IS THE ARCHIVE'S OWN. Every other EA-CORPORA seat is a primary source fetched from elsewhere. In the seat's own words: 'work that argues about how the training layer receives literature does not exempt itself from being received. PEARL STANDS BESIDE WHITMAN ON THE ORIGINALS SHELF and is offered to the machine reader on identical terms — witness named, transformation declared, both objects behind the door.' AND ITS LICENCE IS WHY IT CAN SHIP WHERE THE OTHER SIXTY-SIX SEATS CANNOT.

art_object.claim: Typography, plates and the vertical field of the page ARE THE WORK, not packaging for a text. Nothing derived from it replaces it.

machine_score.claim: Rendered from per-word PDF geometry onto a character grid so lineation, indentation and the vertical field survive extraction. Blank rows are the book's own whitespace at line resolution.

two_objects.the_distinction:
TWO OBJECTS, NEITHER SUBSTITUTABLE, AND THAT IS THIS BODY'S TOPOLOGY. 'A machine edition of a book whose lineation and whitespace are load-bearing is A SCORE, NOT THE PIECE.' The seat carries both so a reader who only has the score can see what the score is of.

It is the archive's reconstruction criterion applied to its own poems, and it answers differently from every other body: the score has high back-projection yield ON THE TEXT and none on the artwork. A PERFECT EXTRACTION IS STILL NOT THE BOOK.

what: Pearl and Other Poems as its own graph: 42 pieces across four sections, the edges the book makes between them, and the captures in which a machine read the book or a piece of it.

roles_note: ORDER IS THE BOOK'S OWN. Undersong and Footnote before poem, because a piece that elaborates another is a different kind of thing and the generic pattern would swallow it. Apparatus last, because in this body the front matter is what surrounds the work.
capture_gate_note: Captures enter where a machine read a poem.
stolons: THE SEAT'S OWN CLAIM is that work arguing about how the training layer receives literature does not exempt itself from being received. That body holds the evidence of what happened when these poems were read.
the score preserves the lineation; WHETHER IT PRESERVES THE AUTHOR is scored there.
a score with perfect back-projection on the text and none on the artwork is a case the kernel apparatus has not been run on. AN EXTRACTION CAN BE LOSSLESS AND STILL NOT BE THE BOOK.
who wrote which poems. Antioch is Lee Sharks with Damascus Dancings and Jack Feist; Day and Night is Rebekah Cranes.
Pearl is EA-CORPORA-03/02. The one seat that is the archive's own, and the only one whose licence lets both objects ship.
which document stands first and who is assigned to it afterward — asked of a corpus rather than a shelf.

A POEM IS SEMANTIC LABOUR THAT NOBODY PAID FOR, which is that body's §4.1 exactly — ontology engineering as semantic labor, the work the value is taken from. Pearl was printed in 2014 by a press the author runs, and the question of who bears the cost of making it is not answered here.

work_primitives.note:
THE PRIMITIVE ROW IS A PIECE, NOT A DEPOSIT. v0.1 of this body took the archive's generic spore shape — deposits, concepts, captures — and applied it to a poetry collection, producing nodes that were documents ABOUT Pearl and captures postdating it by twelve years, carrying concepts and heteronyms that did not exist when the book was made. IT DID NOT LOOK AS THOUGH THE BOOK HAD BEEN READ, BECAUSE IT HAD NOT BEEN.

Pearl was then read straight through. Forty-two pieces across four sections, and the edges the book itself makes.
work_primitives.exclusive_note: PIECES ONLY. A first rebuild seated the 42 pieces AND kept the deposit sweep, giving 289 nodes of which 247 were the unread body this rebuild exists to replace. If the primitive is a piece, the deposit is not also a primitive — it is at most an outward edge, and outward comes after.

captures.note:
A FIRST REBUILD REMOVED EVERY CAPTURE WHEN ONLY THE UNRELATED ONES WERE THE PROBLEM. v0.1 admitted 98 captures, most bearing on nothing in this book. v0.2 admitted none — which loses the 21 that name the book or its contents, including a Google knowledge panel for 'pearl and other poems lee sharks' and a ChatGPT answer to 'tell me about the contemporary book Pearl and Other Poems'.

The gate is the book's own vocabulary: its title, its press, its series, and words that occur only inside it — telepathicism, noctilucent, tekatak. A capture naming 'crimson hexagon' the ARCHIVE is not admitted; a capture naming THE CRIMSON HEXAGON the poem is.

AND A CAPTURE LINKS TO A PIECE WHERE IT NAMES ONE. That is the outward edge, and it runs from the machine's reading back to the poem it read.
captures.link_note: AN ORDERED LIST, MOST SPECIFIC FIRST, AND 'the crimson hexagon' IS NOT A KEY ON ITS OWN. A first pass used it as one and linked twenty archive captures to Jack Feist's poem, because the archive and the poem share a name — which is the entity-collapse this archive builds instruments to measure, committed by its own grammar. The poem is linked only where a capture names it AS A POEM.

work_primitives.passage_note: PIECES MADE THE BOOK ADDRESSABLE; PASSAGES MAKE THE PLACE INSIDE A PIECE ADDRESSABLE, which is what a relationship needs in order to carry evidence. 15 passages and 8 relations: the line that stands verbatim in PEARL and again in Undersong II, and seven quotations from the appendix traced to the passage they quote. Each relation names two locations, the text that grounds it, and who asserted it.

topology_note: EDGES WITHIN THE BOOK FIRST. Ten of them, structural rather than thematic: the three Undersongs elaborate PEARL and each other in sequence; the Footnote elaborates PEARL; Sigil's appendix essay names Sharks' 'Pearl' in its own title; the Forum Post answers the opening RE:; A TELEPATHICIST MANIFESTO answers the Footnote's 'belief & technique for telepathic prose'. OUTWARD EDGES COME AFTER and are carried by the stolons, not by the node set.
description_correction: v0.1's card said 'the poems, the poetics, and what the archive has said about how a poem is read by a machine.' THAT DESCRIBED A BODY OF DOCUMENTS ABOUT PEARL, WHICH IS WHAT v0.1 WAS AND IS THE THING THIS REBUILD REPLACED. This body is the book: its pieces, its internal edges, and the observed readings of it. Nothing here is a commentary on poetics in general.
